{{Quote|Take the shuttle down to fifty meters. And when I exit, you may leave.|Darth Malgus to his pilot|<ref name="Deceived" />}}
A '''shuttle''' was used by the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Malgus]] during, and soon after, the [[Great Galactic War]]. Malgus used the [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] to leave the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]] following a [[Battle of Alderaan|battle]] there. In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[3653 BBY]], shortly after the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith]] [[Sacking of Coruscant|sacked]] the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], he used it again to [[Transport/Legends|transport]] him around the Imperial-occupied planet. The shuttle had a single [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] and an intership [[Comm unit/Legends|comm]].

==Description==
The [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Malgus]]'s personal [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] was operated by a single [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] and could carry at least one passenger. An intership [[Comm unit/Legends|comm unit]] allowed the pilot to communicate with Malgus.<ref name="Deceived" />

==History==
An [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Imperial]] shuttle was used by the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Malgus. After his defeat at the [[Battle of Alderaan]], he was picked up and carried away in his shuttle. While on board the vessel and en route to rendezvous with the rest of the Sith Empire's retreating forces, Malgus sensed a [[Unidentified Zabrak Jedi (Battle of Alderaan)|Jedi]] in the ruins of an [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaanian]] [[City/Legends|city]], and the Sith Lord ordered his pilot to turn around and lower the ship. Malgus overrode the safeties on the [[Entry ramp/Legends|landing ramp]] in order to exit and face the Jedi while the shuttle was still in the air. The shuttle hovered above while Malgus finished his fight.<ref name="Third Lesson">{{InsiderCite|124|The Old Republic: The Third Lesson}}</ref>

Malgus's shuttle was again used shortly after the [[Sacking of Coruscant]]<ref name="Deceived" /> in [[3653 BBY]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' places the ending of the [[Great Galactic War]], which was in the same year as the [[Sacking of Coruscant]], to [[3653 BBY]].</ref> when the Sith Lord was taken to the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. There he planned to confront [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Aryn Leneer]], whom he had been ordered to [[Death/Legends|kill]] by his superior, [[Darth Angral]]. The shuttle circled at an altitude of one hundred [[Meter/Legends|meters]] above the Temple for [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] until Leneer arrived, at which [[Time/Legends|time]] it descended to fifty meters and allowed Malgus to debark and [[Duel in the ruins of the Jedi Temple|face]] Leneer. After Leneer escaped the battle, Malgus recalled his shuttle and was taken to the planet's [[Liston Spaceport]] to intercept the Jedi and to retrieve his lover, [[Eleena Daru]]. During the flight, the back of the shuttle was nearly destroyed by Malgus when his pilot informed him that a [[Treaty of Coruscant|peace accord]] had been reached with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] at the [[Alderaan peace conference]]. As soon as the shuttle arrived at the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]], Malgus bounded off the shuttle in search of Daru.<ref name="Deceived" />

==Commanders and crew==
The shuttle had a single pilot, who [[Transport/Legends|transported]] Darth Malgus where he needed to go.<ref name="Deceived" />

==Behind the scenes==
Darth Malgus's personal shuttle first appeared in [[Paul S. Kemp]]'s short story ''[[The Old Republic: The Third Lesson]]'', which was published in [[Star Wars Insider 124|''Star Wars Insider'' 124]]<ref name="Third Lesson" /> on [[March 2]], [[2011]].<ref name="Date">{{SWArchive|url=vault/books/whatsnewmar14/index.html|text=What's New This Week: ''Insider'' #124, ''Clone Wars Comic'' #6.18, & ''Galaxy'' #6}}</ref>
